chunks: And I found in some of the books a copy of the Book of Gift and Condition from Ar-Rida, Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him), to the officials regarding the matter of Al-Fadl ibn Sahl and his brother, and I did not narrate that from anyone else.

Now then, praise be to God, the Originator, the Able, the Subduer, the Watcher over His servants, the Nourisher of His creatures, to whom all things humble themselves for His dominion, all things yield for His glory, all things submit for His power, all things bow for His sovereignty and greatness, His knowledge encompasses all things and He numbers them, nothing great escapes Him nor any small thing, He whom the eyes of the viewers cannot grasp, and the description of the describers cannot encompass Him, to Him belongs creation and command, and the highest example is in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.

And praise be to God who established Islam as a religion, then favored it, magnified it, honored it, and glorified it, and made it the upright religion that accepts none other, and the straight path that whoever adheres to it does not go astray and whoever turns away from it is not guided, and He placed in it light, proof, healing, and clarity, and sent it by means of those He chose from His angels to those He selected from His messengers among the gone nations and past eras, until his message reached Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), so He concluded with him the prophets and followed with him the traces of the messengers, and sent him as a mercy to the worlds, a bearer of good tidings to the believing affirmers, and a warner to the disbelieving deniers.

So that the conclusive proof may be for Him, and that whoever perishes may perish with clear proof, and whoever lives may live with clear proof, and indeed God is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. And praise be to God who bequeathed to His household the inheritance of prophethood, entrusted them with knowledge and wisdom, made them the source of Imamate and caliphate, made their guardianship obligatory, and honored their status, so He commanded His Messenger to ask his nation for their love, saying: 'Say, I do not ask you for it any reward except love for the near kin,' and what He described them with of removing impurity from them and purifying them, in His saying: 'God only intends to remove from you the impurity, O People of the Household, and purify you with a thorough purification.'

Then indeed Al-Ma'mun honored the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) progeny in his lineage, connected the kinship of the People of the Household, returned their affection, gathered their scattered parts, bridged their gaps, and mended their tears, and God removed through him the animosities and grudges between them, and settled mutual support, continuity, love, and affection in their hearts, so by his blessing, protection, barakah, piety, and kinship, their hands became one, their word became united, and their inclinations agreed.

He observed the rights for their owners and placed the inheritances in their places, rewarded the good of the good-doers, preserved the test of the tested, brought near and kept far those based on religion, then he distinguished with preference, precedence, and honor whoever his efforts had advanced, and that was Thul-Riasatayn (The Two Excellences), Al-Fadl ibn Sahl.

For he saw him as a supporter for him, standing by his right, speaking with his proof, a leader for his nobles, a commander for his cavalry, a manager for his wars, a ruler for his subjects, a caller to him, rewarding those who answered his obedience, opposing those who stubbornly turned away, unique in his victory, and a healer for the sickness of hearts and intentions.

Not the lack of wealth nor the shortage of men deterred him from that, nor did greed incline him, nor did anything divert him from his intention and insight, but rather, when those who frighten frighten and those who thunder and flash thunder and flash, and the multitude of opponents and resistors from the fighters and the cunning, he was most firm in resolve, most courageous in spirit, most piercing in stratagem, best in management, and strongest in steadfastness regarding the right of Al-Ma'mun and the call to him.

Until he broke the fangs of misguidance, blunted their edge, clipped their nails, harvested their thorns, and struck them down with the strikes of the atheists in his religion, the breakers of his covenant, the faltering in his affair, the轻视 of his right, the secure from what he warned of of his onslaught and might, along with the traces of Thul-Riasatayn among the various nations of the polytheists, and what God increased through him in the boundaries of the abode of the Muslims, the news of which has reached you, and the books were read on your pulpits, and the people of the horizons carried from you to others.

So the gratitude of Thul-Riasatayn reached the test of the Commander of the Faithful with him, and his standing by his right, and his spending of his life and the life of his brother, Abu Muhammad Al-Hasan ibn Sahl, the blessed, the noble, the praiseworthy in politics, to a limit that he surpassed the predecessors and excelled the winners by it.

And the reward of the Commander of the Faithful for him reached what he made for him of wealth, estates, and jewels, although that did not suffice for a day of his days or a position of his positions, so he left it out of asceticism in it, and elevation of his spirit from it, and sufficiency for him over the Muslims, and casting aside of the world and belittling it, and preference for the Hereafter and competition in it.

And he asked the Commander of the Faithful what he had not ceased asking and desiring from him of retirement and asceticism, so that became great with him and with us due to our knowledge of what God, the Exalted, placed in its place, which is of honor for the religion and the authority, and strength for the rectification of the Muslims and the jihad of the polytheists, and what God saw in it of confirming his intention, the blessing of his nobility, the soundness of his management, the strength of his opinion, the success of his seeking, and his assistance with the truth, guidance, piety, and God-consciousness.

So when the Commander of the Faithful trusted him, and we trusted him regarding the care of the religion and preferring what is in it for its rectification, we gave him his request which befits his rank, and wrote for him the Book of Gift and Condition, which is copied at the bottom of this book of mine, and we made God witness over it, and those who were present with us from our household, the commanders, the companions, the judges, the jurists, the elite, and the commoners.

And the Commander of the Faithful deemed it proper to send the book to the horizons so that it may spread and circulate among its people, be read on their pulpits, and be established with their governors and judges, so he asked me to write that and explain its meanings, and they are on three chapters.

So in the first chapter, the explanation of all his traces by which God made his right obligatory upon us and upon the Muslims. And the second chapter, the explanation of his rank in removing the cause in all that he managed and entered into, and there is no way for him in what he left and disliked, and that is what is not for any creation among those who have a pledge on their neck except for him alone and his brother. And from the removal of the cause is their arbitration in all who were wronged by them and sought corruption against us and against them and against our allies, so that no one may hope for opposition to them or disobedience to them or trickery in an entry between us and them.

And the third chapter, the explanation of our giving him what he liked of the ownership of retirement and the adornment of asceticism and the proof of verification for what he sought of the reward of the Hereafter, by what becomes settled in the heart of those who were in that from him, and what is obligatory upon us for him of honor and glory, and the gift that we bestowed upon him and his brother of preventing them from what we prevent ourselves from, and that encompasses all that is encompassed in the precaution of a matter of religion and world.

And this is the copy of the book: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. This is a book and condition from Abdullah Al-Ma'mun, Commander of the Faithful, and his successor Ali ibn Musa, to Thul-Riasatayn Al-Fadl ibn Sahl, on the day of Monday for seven days remaining of the month of Ramadan from the year two hundred and one.

And it is the day on which God perfected the dominion of the Commander of the Faithful, and concluded for his successor, and clothed the people with the green garment, and reached his hope in the rectification of his successor and victory over his enemy. We called you to that in which is some of your reward for what you did of the right of God, the Blessed, the Exalted, and the right of His Messenger, and the right of the Commander of the Faithful and his successor Ali ibn Musa, and the right of Hashim by which the rectification of the religion and the safety of the bond between the Muslims is hoped.

Until the blessing was established upon us and upon the public by that and by what you assisted the Commander of the Faithful with of establishing the religion and the sunnah, and manifesting the second call, and preferring the first with the suppression of polytheism, the breaking of idols, and killing the rebels, and all your traces represented in the cities in the deposed one, and in the one named Asfar, known as Abu al-Saraya, and in the one named Al-Mahdi, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tabari, and the Khalaji Turks.

And in Tabaristan and its kings to Bunder, Hormuz ibn Shirwin, and in Daylam and its king, and in Kabul and its king, the Mahwazin, then its king, Asfahbud, and in Ibn al-Baram, and the mountains of Badarbandeh, Garsistan, and Ghor and its types, and in Khorasan, the Khagan, and Maloon, the owner of Jabal al-Tabbat, and in Kerman and at-Taqraqar, and in Arminiyah and Hijaz, and the owner of As-Sarir and the owner of al-Khazar, and in Maghrib and his wars.

And the explanation of that is in the Diwan of the Sirah. And what we called you to, which is assistance for you, is one hundred thousand thousand dirhams, and the yield of ten thousand thousand dirhams in jewels, besides what the Commander of the Faithful had granted you before, and the value of one hundred thousand thousand dirhams in jewels is little compared to what you are deserving of.

So you left like that when the deposed one bestowed it upon you, and you preferred God and His religion, and indeed you thanked the Commander of the Faithful and his successor, and you preferred the sufficiency of all that over the Muslims, and you gave it to them, and you asked us that the characteristic which you have constantly yearned for of asceticism and retirement reach you.

So that your leaving the world may be correct with those who doubted in your striving for the Hereafter rather than the world, and what is not dispensed with like you in any state, and like you is not turned away from his request, even if our request takes us from half the blessings upon us, so how about a matter in which the burden is raised and the proof is made obligatory upon those who claim that your call to us is for the world, not the Hereafter.

And we have answered you to what you asked, and made that for you confirmed by the covenant of God and His pledge, which has no change and no alteration, and we delegated the matter in its time to you, so whatever you remain, you are mighty, the removal of the cause is pushed away from you, the entry into what you dislike of actions, whatever it be, we prevent you from what we prevent ourselves from in all states.

And when you desire retirement, the removal of the body is honored, and rest and honor are a right for your body, then we give you what you take from what we bestowed upon you in this book, which you left today, and we made for Al-Hasan ibn Sahl what we made for you, and half of what we bestowed of the gift.

And the people of that are for you, and by what he spent of himself in the jihad of the rebels and the conquest of Iraq twice, and the dispersal of the hosts of Satan by his hands, until the religion became strong, and he waded through the fire of wars, as a fulfillment and thanks with himself and his household and whoever he ruled from the allies of the truth.

And we made God witness over us, and His angels, and the best of His creation, and everyone who gave us his pledge and the clapping of his right hand on this day and after it, regarding what is in this book, and we made God our guarantor, and made it obligatory upon ourselves to fulfill what we stipulated without exception of anything that breaks it in secret and in public.

And the believers are upon their conditions, and the covenant is an obligation to be questioned, and the people most entitled to fulfillment is he who asks the people for fulfillment and is a place for power, for indeed God, the Blessed, the Exalted, says: 'And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant, and do not break the oaths after their confirmation, and you have made God over you a guarantor. Indeed God knows what you do.'

And Al-Hasan ibn Sahl wrote the signature of Al-Ma'mun in it: In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. The Commander of the Faithful has made obligatory upon himself all that is in this book, and made God witness, the Blessed, the Exalted, and made Him a caller and guarantor over it, and wrote with his hand in Safar, the year two hundred and two, to honor the gift and confirm the condition.

The signature of Ar-Rida (peace be upon him): In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful. Ali ibn Musa has obligated upon himself all that is in the book, according to what was confirmed in it, from his day and tomorrow, as long as he lives, and made God over him a guardian and guarantor, and sufficient is God as a witness, and he wrote with his hand in this month of this year. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. And blessings be upon Muhammad and his family, and peace. And sufficient for us is God, and He is the best trustee.

key_terms.الْحِبَاء وَالشَّرْط: Gift and Condition (a formal contract of appointment and reward)
key_terms.الْعِلَّة: The cause/obstacle (referring to removing impediments to authority)
key_terms.ذُو الرِّئَاسَتَيْنِ: The Two Excellences (a title for Al-Fadl ibn Sahl)

ai.seo_question: What were the terms and conditions of Al-Fadl ibn Sahl's appointment as prime minister according to the Book of Gift and Condition?
ai.summary: This document, preserved by Shaykh al-Saduq, details the political and spiritual dynamics of Imam al-Rida’s (a.s.) acceptance of Caliph Al-Ma'mun’s designation, highlighting the strategic appointment of Al-Fadl ibn Sahl as 'Thul-Riasatayn' (Possessor of the Two Authorities) to consolidate Abbasid power while validating the Imamate. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Imam’s presence in the court was a divine mandate to preserve the truth amidst political turmoil, with the 'Gift and Condition' serving as a formal covenant of mutual rights and spiritual authority. The text emphasizes that despite the worldly honors bestowed, the Imam’s ultimate goal remained the preservation of religious integrity and the guidance of the faithful.
